text: Does a Gaussian wave packet in v (amplitude 4, width sigma=1.5, centered at x=-5) with u=0 decompose into a soliton train of >=2 well-separated peaks each with amplitude >=0.8 in the coupled Burgers-swept-KdV system, and does mass(v) drift stay below 8%?

method: Fourier pseudospectral + 2/3-rule dealiasing on all nonlinear products + classical RK4 (fully explicit, no IMEX)
bank_use_rationale: BKdV-S1 deep synthesis confirms Fourier+2/3+RK4 is the working stack for BKdV at amp<=3; I adopt it as the baseline with dt=1e-4 (more conservative than validated dt=2e-4) to handle amplitude-4 IC. Rejected IMEX and IFRK4 because kb-gardner-G4 and kb-gardner-nonlinearCFL-amplitude-boundary show IMEX nonlinear CFL blows up at high amplitudes (max|6v+1.5v^2|=48 at A=4 vs 12.4 at A=1.5); rejected no-dealiasing per BKdV-S1 (blowup before t=0.5) and kb-kdv-noDealiasing.

rationale: Run completed in ~14s with no NaN/Inf. 12 prominent peaks (height>=0.8, prominence>=0.5) in v at T=6, well above the required >=2. Mass drift is exactly 0.0% (spectral divergence-form conservation). The Gaussian IC decomposes into a rich multi-peak train consistent with KdV-type soliton decomposition. Phenomenon target met.

F1 is fully positive: 12 well-separated peaks each with amplitude >=0.8, mass drift=0%, all finite. Phenomenon target (>=2 peaks >=0.8, mass drift <8%) is met with large margin. No further iteration needed.
